name: Two Knights Defense — White Tactics
description: 4 tactical challenges for White in the Two Knights Defense. Find the winning 2-move sequence from the critical positions after both sides have castled.

drills.name: e-file Pin & Overload
drills.description: White doubles on the e-file and pins the knight on e7.
drills.briefExplanation: Re1 reloads the rook on the open e-file. When Black centralises the knight, Qe2 adds overwhelming pressure.
drills.explanation: Qe2 adds decisive pressure. White continues with 16.Bg5 (pinning) and 17.Bxe7, winning the knight or forcing Black to ruin their pawn structure. The e-file battery — rook on e1, queen on e2 — becomes an unstoppable force targeting the pinned Ne7.

drills.name: f7 Sacrifice
drills.description: White sacrifices the knight to destroy Black's king cover.
drills.briefExplanation: Nxf7 tears apart Black's kingside. After Rxf7, White crashes through on e7 with the rook.
drills.explanation: Rxe7 wins the exchange. White follows with 16.Qh5 and 17.Re1, targeting the exposed king and winning decisive material. The f7 sacrifice is a classic in all Italian Game positions — the knight forks queen and rook, and even after recapture White has devastating compensation.

drills.name: d6 Breakthrough
drills.description: White pushes the d-pawn to cramp Black and open lines.
drills.briefExplanation: d6 wedges deep into Black's position. After Nxd6, Re1 seizes the e-file and attacks the exposed knight.
drills.explanation: Re1 supports the pawn and attacks the Nd6 immediately. White continues with 16.Bf4 and 17.Qd2, creating a powerful passed pawn and attacking the e7-knight. The d6-pawn disrupts Black's coordination and gives White a lasting initiative.

drills.name: Bg5 Pin Exploitation
drills.description: White pins the knight on f6 and prepares to destroy Black's kingside.
drills.briefExplanation: Bg5 pins the bishop on f6 to the queen. Even after h6, White takes anyway — the structural damage is worth it.
drills.explanation: Bxf6 damages Black's pawn structure. White follows with 16.Qh5 and 17.Re1, targeting h7 and f7 for a decisive kingside attack. The bishop pair is surrendered in exchange for wrecking Black's kingside — a classic exchange in all Italian Game attacking positions.
